title: It works, but not the greatest
text:
It works, but not the greatest. We're avid tea drinkers who work urns like these pretty hard, they often get left on for days at a time so we have hot water ready especially in the cold winter months. I have to say, this unit is pretty standard, but seems rather cheaply made. For starters, the spout seems to take FOREVER to pour into a cup. Other urns we've owned can fill a mug with piping hot water in about 5 seconds, this one feels like it takes at least double that time if not longer. It might not seem like much, but when you're making tea for 3-4 people, the difference becomes frustratingly noticeable. Next thing I noticed is that the cord is insanely short. We had to get an extension cord to reach the nearest outlet. I've never owned one this short before.
Then there's the logo. I'll admit, this is purely aesthetic but I kind of hate the logo. It looks so out of place and in a bizarre font that just seems somewhat cringe worthy. The good news is, it seems very cheaply printed onto the metal and actually comes off with a FINGERNAIL scratching at it. That's good and bad however- its good because I was able to remove it easily with my thumb nail, but it also makes me wonder what would happen to this if exposed to the heat of the unit running for a prolonged amount of time. Like, would it burn off and/or smell? If it comes off that easily I don't have high confidence in the quality of the printing. Then there's the temperature. I don't know exactly how hot it is, but it seems less hot than some of the other urns we've used. For things like tea and instant oatmeal, its fine but when I made coffee and then added cold milk, it already lost the piping hot effect I was hoping to have to warm me up in the morning. It simply isn't starting off hot enough to add cold milk to it and remain hot.
In a nutshell, it works and does what it claims to do. But for the money, I think there are better options out there.
